examples.solution_text:
(a) Multiply the numbers, then the pronumerals.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}-5m\times4n\\&=(-5\times4)(m\times n)\\&=-20mn\end{aligned}$
(b)
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}3p\times2p\\&=(3\times2)(p\times p)\\&=6p^2\end{aligned}$

Multiply all three coefficients and show the repeated pronumeral.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}(-2a)\times3a\times4b\\&=(-2\times3\times4)(a\times a)b\\&=-24a^2b\end{aligned}$

(a) Write the division as a fraction and divide top and bottom by $7$.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}14t\div21\\&=\frac{14t}{21}\\&=\frac{2t}{3}\end{aligned}$
(b) Divide top and bottom by $6$. The $q$ stays in the denominator.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\frac{18}{12q}\\&=\frac{3}{2q}\end{aligned}$

(a) Cancel the common factors $5$, $u$ and $v$.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\frac{15u^2v}{10uv}\\&=\frac{3u}{2}\end{aligned}$
(b) Cancel the common factors $4$ and $s$. One factor of $s$ remains in the denominator.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\frac{-8s}{12s^2}\\&=-\frac{2}{3s}\end{aligned}$

(a) Multiply the numbers, then the pronumerals. The repeated factor is $b$.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}-4ab\times5bc\\&=(-4\times5)a(b\times b)c\\&=-20ab^2c\end{aligned}$
(b) Divide top and bottom by the common factor $5rs$.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\frac{30r^2s^3}{5rs}\\&=\frac{6\times5\times r\times r\times s\times s\times s}{5\times r\times s}\\&=6rs^2\end{aligned}$

examples.derivation: (-5)(4)mn=-20mn; (3)(2)pp=6p^2. These follow the supplied multiplication examples. Formatting preserves the original mathematics and adds correct invisible opening gutters.
(-2)(3)(4)=-24 and a×a×b=a^2b, giving -24a^2b. The supplied exercises support three-term multiplication. Formatting preserves all original steps.
Dividing 14t and 21 by 7 gives 2t/3. Dividing 18 and 12q by 6 gives 3/(2q), with q nonzero. Both use the supplied numerical cancellation method; splitting the equality preserves the mathematics.
Cancelling 5uv from 15u^2v/(10uv) gives 3u/2. Cancelling 4s from -8s/(12s^2) gives -2/(3s). Stated nonzero conditions permit cancellation. Formatting preserves both original solutions.
(-4)(5)a×b×b×c=-20ab^2c. Expanding 30r^2s^3 into factors and cancelling 5rs gives 6rs^2. Both are different-value adaptations of the cited booklet exercises, within the assessed methods.
